title: Roast celeriac and chickpeas with tahini

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a simple single-ingredient staple; tahini is just ground sesame and is on the store cupboard list.

supermarket.reason: Celeriac, kale, tinned chickpeas, tahini and pumpkin seeds are all everyday Tesco lines at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a small bowl and a whisk, and the technique is simple roasting.

works.reason: A whole celeriac with two tins of chickpeas feeds four, and 36 minutes at 220°C will roast the cubes tender with crisp kale; the lemon and seasoning are clear enough to judge by taste.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers peeling and cubing the celeriac, cutting the onion wedges, tearing the kale, slicing the apple and making the dressing, and the 20+10+6 roasting adds up to the 36 minutes printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, including pepper in 'Season' and lemon in the dressing, and nothing unlisted is used except water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm roast celeriac traybake suits mid-November, and the celeriac is the bulk and point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Roast vegetables, chickpeas, kale and a tahini dressing make a filling, real-food lunch with protein and plenty of veg.
